title: MX Coprocessor Clock Glitch FI — Complete Results

sweet_spot_persistent.effect: FPGA config SRAM bit-flip, ret=27 (golden=25), XOR=0x2
sweet_spot_persistent.note: Persistent until reprogram. Same bit flipped every trial.

scan_readout.fields: rs1_q, rs2_q, mac_acc, se_a, se_b, op, fmt, inflight, rd, id

bitstream_2_with_scan.no_effect: w=-9 and above (0 crashes, 0 faults in 1500+ trials)

scan_difference_at_w8.cycle_98: golden se=254,30 → faulted se=255,255 (60 bits diff)
scan_difference_at_w8.cycle_173: golden zeros → faulted se_b=120 (28 bits diff)
scan_difference_at_w8.note: Glitch shifts timing of captured instruction, not corruption

bitstream_2_with_scan.limitation: CW-Lite integer width: gap between w=-9 (no effect) and w=-10 (crash) too wide for silent fault

infrastructure_proven.scan_auto_capture: REG 0x0D scan_delay, captures at programmable cycle after trigger

next_steps: Husky with fractional width for silent fault sweet spot
Higher clock frequency (30-40 MHz) to narrow timing margins
Different firmware with longer MX computation for more glitch windows
